turns.zh: 是的，我认为大致就是这样运作的。我们认为我们的同事在使用产品以及使用智能体产品方面品味很高。因此，对于我们构建的许多东西，我们会在内部发布，并从每天使用它们的公司其他人那里获得反馈，寻找内部 PMF。通常，这对于向更广泛的世界发布一些东西是一个好迹象。所以 Grok Bot 遵循了完全相同的流程。不过，我认为 Grok Bot 真正独特的地方在于，就像我之前说的，无论角色如何，从运营到市场到插入你的角色，有人找到了 Grok Bot 的用例，很大程度上是因为它与您已经使用的所有工具无缝对话，然后显然就像 Lauren 说的，它有自己的电脑，所以它是一种持久性智能体，与之交互感觉非常新颖，所以我认为其中一些交互，希望我们稍后能展示给你看，非常非常酷。

turns.en: All right let's jump in. I feel like I got all of the preview. I'm ready to jump into the demo. Let's take it away.

So here's my coordinate agent messaging shopppee who helps me buy stuff on the internet and learning about the recent purchases I just made
turns.zh: 是的。我可以开始，也许我们可以稍微来回一下。所以你现在看到的是 Grok Bot，这是我的一队机器人。我这里有一个协调智能体，他是我的参谋长，了解我的日历，并且可以给我的其他智能体发消息，所以可以检查其他智能体的进展。所以这是我的协调智能体在给 shopppee 发消息，shopppee 帮助我在网上买东西，并了解我最近的购买。

turns.en: So Grok 4.6 is really powerful. It's much more intelligent than 4.5 at the same token cost. So I think for coding tasks and the type of work that I do, because I do a lot of engineering work, I use Grok 4.6 a lot for that, and it's just way more capable. It's really, really fast.

turns.en: And so, yeah, we're just excited for the models to keep improving, to be part of the discussion on the frontier of models, and to be able to bring that into the world.
turns.zh: 所以，我们很期待模型持续进步，期待参与前沿模型的讨论，也期待把这些带到现实世界里。

turns.en: And then I realized, before I was actually testing out Grok Bot, I was like, oh, you can use this same tool to do research, to do other things. And then of course some of the design touches that we added over time.
turns.zh: 嗯，其实需求很简单，就是保持简洁。说得俏皮一点，我觉得这真的很实在。很多 AI 应用给了你很多控制和能力，但有时候这种能力是和复杂性相平衡的。所以我们这里的设计需求就是：首先，怎么把它做得非常简单？所以消息式的界面多少是从这里得到启发的。当然，还有我们后来陆续加的一些设计细节。

turns.zh: 我不敢说我把它全做出来了，但我觉得团队确实在追求一个非常干净、简洁的用户界面，因为如果你用过 Cursor，你大概是个资深开发者、资深用户。它非常——有很多开关和花哨的功能，非常针对编程场景定制。

turns.zh: 而做 Grok 时，我们真的很想换一个全新的视角：如果你的智能体更像一个同事，会是什么样子？对吧？你不一定想事无巨细地管着一个同事，问他“你现在在调用什么工具？”而是想把它当人一样对话。

turns.zh: 对。你想看到他们在电脑上做什么。所以，我们尽量让界面保持优雅和简洁。

I think that inspired some of the thinking behind Grok Bot—like, what if everybody could define one of their own bots, give it an identity, and give it things like its own computer plus routines and automations? So like I have life bots right now that are—every time someone gives us feedback on Grok Bot, my bots are automatically going off and fixing them for me, and I just review their code.
turns.zh: 这就是我们早期实验的灵感来源，我们想做一个更持久的机器人。我觉得我们从那里借鉴了一些想法，因为很多人问我：你是怎么建的？我怎么能建自己的？这启发了 Grok Bot 背后的一些思考——如果每个人都能定义自己的机器人，给它一个身份，给它自己的电脑、例行程序和自动化，会怎样？所以我现在有生活机器人，每当有人给 Grok Bot 反馈，我的机器人就会自动去修，我只需要审查它们的代码。

turns.zh: 是的。所以我之前已经问了我的幕僚长，今天有没有看到什么有趣的 bug。它找到了几个。你也可以看到，我在机器人的电脑上打开了 X，以防万一。但是的，你知道，我可以让它派发任务。所以我这里有一个沙团队——抱歉，一个 Grok Bot 团队。他们每个人负责不同的功能。现在我的幕僚长要把这些任务发给那些智能体。过一会儿我们会看到它发给不同团队成员的一堆消息。然后它们会去实际处理那些任务。最后我会收到一个可以审查的拉取请求。我会收到视频，所以我会收到截图。嗯，是的。所以这里还有一个例子，这是我工程团队的一个智能体。我觉得这几乎是一个不太明显的功能，但如果你在 Cursor 上设置了云智能体，你的 Grok Bot 机器人实际上可以启动它们。

turns.en: So like here, you know, we have—like I have a cloud agent that's running with its own computer that this agent is managing. And so it's got like a bunch of things in flight already, so I have a bunch of PRs to review later.
turns.zh: 所以就像这里，你知道，我们有一个——我有一个云智能体，它用自己的电脑运行，而这个智能体在管理它。所以它已经有一堆任务在进行中，我稍后有一堆 PR 要审查。

turns.zh: 我觉得这里也展现了软件开发未来的一个非常令人兴奋的方向：你实际上是在与一群执行特定任务的智能体交谈和协作，然后你退后一步，成为它们的管理者。感觉那个愿景在这里以一种非常有趣的方式成真了。所以是的。

turns.zh: 是的，我就是喜欢猫。所以我决定给它们一些傻傻的头像。只是为了给我的 Grok Bot 一点个性化。默认的 Grok Bot 头像也超级可爱。我是在我们添加那些之前加的。但就是图个乐子，你知道。

turns.en: Yeah, Roshan, you hinted towards something that is a trend that of course is happening with the future of agent coding, and Cursor has been at the front and center of seeing all of this happen. More and more code is getting automated and is done by these agents, and so as a human you become this puppeteer of agents who are handling all these tasks for you. I know that's a world that you're particularly excited about. Can you share a little bit more why are you excited about that? What does that actually unlock at maybe the human level that people in the mainstream audience might not realize?
turns.zh: 是的，Roshan，你暗示了一个趋势，这当然是智能体编程未来正在发生的，而 Cursor 一直处于见证这一切发生的前沿和中心。越来越多的代码被自动化，由这些智能体完成，所以作为人类，你成了这些智能体的木偶师，它们为你处理所有这些任务。我知道那是你特别兴奋的世界。你能多分享一点为什么你对此感到兴奋吗？这在人类层面上实际解锁了什么，主流观众可能没有意识到？

turns.en: Yeah, totally. I think if I had to pick one word, it would be efficiency. I think there's so many ideas in people's heads regardless of role—again, like I have so many product ideas I want to build into Cursor. And it's the limiting factor—like there's always some bottleneck in that idea-to-existence pipeline. And so I think the promise of being able to throw fleets of agents at these problems and then have them produce things that are really high quality and sort of align with the taste that I would myself put into our product—that's the vision, right? Like that's sort of the dream. It's like being able to go from thought to existence. So to me that's the thing to work towards—is can we build these things in a way where whether I'm managing a bunch of agents or asking agents to manage other agents or working with Lauren's agents or whatever that looks like—we're able to really shorten, compress, compress, compress that cycle more and more. And I think if you look at the evolution of Cursor as a company, that's sort of how we've built ourselves towards that future in a lot of ways—by continuing to introduce more and more agent tools and complexity there. So yeah, I think that's the vision and we're excited for it.
turns.zh: 是的，完全同意。我觉得如果用一个词概括，那就是效率。不管什么角色，人们脑子里都有很多想法——比如我有很多产品想法想构建到 Cursor 里。而限制因素就是——从想法到存在的流程中总会有瓶颈。所以我认为，能够向这些问题投入大量智能体，然后让它们产出真正高质量、并且符合我自己会放入产品中的品味的东西——那就是愿景，对吧？就像那个梦想。就是从思想到存在。所以对我来说，要努力的方向就是——我们能不能以这样的方式构建这些东西：无论是我管理一堆智能体，还是让智能体管理其他智能体，或者与 Lauren 的智能体合作，或者不管是什么形式——我们都能真正地缩短、压缩、再压缩那个周期，越来越短。而且我认为如果你看看 Cursor 作为一家公司的演变，那就是我们在很多方面朝着那个未来构建自己的方式——通过不断引入越来越多的智能体工具和复杂性。所以是的，我认为那就是愿景，我们对此感到兴奋。

turns.en: And then how has it changed on the software engineering team? What differences from when you started working at Cursor to how it is now?
turns.zh: 那么软件工程团队发生了怎样的变化？从你开始在 Cursor 工作到现在，有什么不同？

turns.en: I think the way I see engineers' roles evolve in the agent world is, like I mentioned, you're sort of like an engineering manager for your agents. But I think a big part of our responsibility now as engineers is also to keep the codebase in a condition where product managers and designers can contribute high-quality code. That's something I talk a lot about on Twitter as well, which is investing in refactoring, rewriting, even rewriting your codebase so that agents can really thrive even if they're not very smart sometimes. Things like encoding your rules and your style guides into actual lint rules or hard constraints that fail CI. So again, I think the big unlock is that as an engineer I can empower so many other people to do things that they couldn't do before, and I can do things that I couldn't do before as well. Because I've done a lot of big refactors and migrations at Cursor and I did them mostly by myself with one other cat agent.
turns.zh: 我认为在智能体世界里，工程师的角色演变就像我提到的，你有点像你智能体的工程经理。但我觉得现在作为工程师，我们很大一部分责任也是保持代码库处于一种状态，让产品经理和设计师也能贡献高质量的代码。这也是我在 Twitter 上经常谈到的，就是投资于重构、重写，甚至重写你的代码库，这样即使智能体有时不那么聪明，它们也能真正茁壮成长。比如把你的规则和风格指南编码成实际的 lint 规则或硬性约束，让 CI 失败。所以再次强调，我认为最大的突破是，作为工程师，我可以赋能很多其他人去做他们以前做不到的事情，同时我也能做以前做不到的事情。因为我在 Cursor 做了很多大型重构和迁移，我 mostly 都是自己做的，还有一个猫智能体。

turns.en: Yeah, all the cat agents were just going wild and I converted a bunch of stuff which would have taken me or a team of engineers months or even years to finish.
turns.zh: 是的，所有的猫智能体都疯狂运行，我转换了一大堆东西，这本来会花费我或一个工程师团队几个月甚至几年的时间来完成。

turns.en: Wow, that's incredible. And as an outsider's perspective, you might think, okay, now that agents can do all this coding, what's the role of a software engineer? And if you actually look at what's happening on the ground, there's more demand than ever for more and more of these engineers. And it's probably towards something that you hinted now that you can build software with the thought to execution timeline is getting so condensed. We just now get something like Grok Bot that started off as that's something you guys are building and then you could use Grok Bot to now build Grok Bot and put it out into commercial production. Is that also what you're seeing just as a trend happen more and more?
turns.zh: 哇，太不可思议了。从外行人的角度来看，你可能会想，好吧，既然智能体能做所有这些编码，软件工程师的角色是什么？但如果你实际看看地面上发生的事情，对更多这类工程师的需求比以往任何时候都大。这可能朝着你暗示的方向发展，现在你可以构建软件，从想法到执行的时间线变得如此压缩。我们现在有了像 Grok Bot 这样的东西，它最初是你们在构建的，然后你可以用 Grok Bot 来构建 Grok Bot 并将其投入商业生产。这也是你看到的趋势吗，越来越普遍？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean I think the time to prototype ideas has gone down a bunch and so it's really quick to test things. I think we've been able, like the team behind Grok Bot has been able to move incredibly quickly just because of these tools getting better. And obviously the models getting better is a huge component of that. And so, yeah, I think that like to bring it to the Grok Bot side of things, the motivation there is really around how can we make this product more and more helpful for folks. As far as the trend, I think this is going to get easier. I think there's still a really strong role for people to play in all that too, right? Whether it's the taste argument or some other combination like that. But yeah, I think it's just ideas are abound and it's just going to be exciting to see more and more of them come to reality.
turns.zh: 是的，我认为原型想法的时间大大缩短了，所以测试东西非常快。我认为我们能够——就像 Grok Bot 背后的团队能够以令人难以置信的速度前进，只是因为这些工具变得更好。显然，模型变得更好是其中很大的一部分。所以，是的，我认为就 Grok Bot 而言，动机真的是围绕如何让这个产品对人们越来越有帮助。至于趋势，我认为这会变得更容易。我认为人们在其中仍然扮演着非常重要的角色，对吧？无论是品味论证还是其他类似的组合。但是的，我认为想法比比皆是，看到越来越多的想法成为现实将令人兴奋。

turns.en: Wow, that's yeah, the sort of analogy or metaphor that I personally like a lot is this idea that—so I like food. I'm a big lover of food. And I kind of think of my agents as sort of like a kitchen, a Michelin kitchen is what I call it. And so maybe my role has sort of changed in that maybe I'm not cooking all the food myself anymore. But I have a team of bots and agents that I've sort of hired, right? And I've trained through skills or refactoring to do good code the way that I would have done it. And so my role is becoming more like a head chef, right? Like I maybe assemble a plate of food. I own the quality control. But if you invest a lot in having a really capable team of agents, you can just do so much more. And now think about that with every engineer in your team can have one of these teams behind them, you can really solve a lot more problems. You know, you can build more features. Not all of them should be built, but you have much more productivity and velocity.
turns.zh: 哇，是的，我个人非常喜欢的一个类比或隐喻是这个想法——我喜欢食物。我是个大美食家。我有点把我的智能体想象成一个厨房，我称之为米其林厨房。所以也许我的角色有点变化，也许我不再自己烹饪所有的食物。但我有一队机器人和智能体，我有点像雇佣了他们，对吧？我通过技能或重构训练他们以我会做的方式写出好代码。所以我的角色变得更像主厨，对吧？我可能组装一盘食物。我负责质量控制。但如果你投入很多拥有一个真正有能力的智能体团队，你可以做更多的事情。现在想想，你团队中的每个工程师都可以拥有这样一个团队在他们背后，你真的可以解决更多问题。你知道，你可以构建更多功能。不是所有功能都应该构建，但你有更高的生产力和速度。

turns.en: Yeah, I do like what you hinted about the internal culture of you actually build things, you test it out and that the employees themselves at Cursor have a certain taste for what other engineers, what other product people would, other consumers I guess in general would want to see exist. Do you have any hints that you can maybe share—okay if you don't—but of what might be coming up or even something that people are working on internally?
turns.zh: 是的，我确实喜欢你暗示的内部文化，你实际构建东西，测试它，而且 Cursor 的员工本身对其他工程师、其他产品人员、我想其他消费者一般会希望看到什么存在有一定的品味。你有没有什么提示可以分享——好吧，如果你没有的话——关于可能即将出现的东西，甚至人们内部正在做的事情？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean we definitely want to make Grok Bot better. We launched this as a beta yesterday and so tons of feedback coming in of all shapes and sizes. Our goal there is just to make this as helpful—these assistants, these bots—as helpful as we can and so definitely going to continue investing there. Obviously really excited about the models getting better too and excited to be a part of that conversation and to have frontier models now. And so I think we're going to continue to just invest a bunch in that space and then some more fun stuff to come too. But I think overall just very bullish on the future and the future of both coding agents but also as general purpose agents and I think it's going to be a really fun time.
turns.zh: 是的，我们肯定想使 Grok Bot 更好。我们昨天作为测试版发布了这个，所以收到了大量各种形式的反馈。我们的目标只是让这些助手、这些机器人尽可能有帮助，所以肯定会继续在那里投资。显然也很兴奋模型变得更好，并兴奋能参与那个对话，现在拥有前沿模型。所以我认为我们将继续在那个领域投入大量资金，然后还有一些更有趣的东西会来。但总体而言，我只是对未来非常看好，无论是编码智能体还是通用智能体的未来，我认为这将是一个非常有趣的时期。

turns.en: Definitely. Yeah. I'm personally really excited to see more performance and reliability as an engineer. That's something I care about a lot. But yeah, we have some really interesting features that we're debating. Like one thing that I tried to hack in—I hacked into Grok Bot in the early days—was support for iMessage. You can actually text your bots. I don't know if we'll add it for Grok Bot but I know it's a common ask. But we're definitely thinking about things like this where again the mental model is these are colleagues, right? So how do you make your colleague accessible not just through Slack, right? You can text them, you can call them. So it's interesting to imagine a world where you have these always-on colleagues that you can talk to at any time from anywhere and they're just off doing work for you.
turns.zh: 当然。是的。我个人非常兴奋看到作为工程师的更多性能和可靠性。这是我非常关心的事情。但是的，我们有一些非常有趣的功能正在讨论。比如我早期尝试在 Grok Bot 中黑客的一个功能是支持 iMessage。你实际上可以给你的机器人发短信。我不知道我们是否会为 Grok Bot 添加它，但我知道这是一个常见的要求。但我们肯定在考虑这样的事情，再次，心智模型是这些是同事，对吧？那么如何让你的同事不仅通过 Slack 可以访问，对吧？你可以给他们发短信，你可以打电话给他们。所以想象一个世界，你有这些永远在线的同事，你可以随时随地与他们交谈，他们只是在外为你工作，这很有趣。

turns.en: Oh my gosh, I can't wait to be able to text them or call them. I saw this meme where it's like my agents were talking to each other in their stand-up and they're like, 'Sorry, I was off all weekend.' It's like you're an agent. Like I don't know exactly what that means.
turns.zh: 天哪，我迫不及待想能给他们发短信或打电话。我看到这个梗，就像我的智能体在站会上互相交谈，他们说：‘抱歉，我整个周末都休息了。’就像你是个智能体。我不知道那到底是什么意思。

turns.en: Yeah, maybe we need agent PTO as a frontier.
turns.zh: 是的，也许我们需要智能体带薪休假作为前沿。

turns.en: Agent PTO, turn your computer off.
turns.zh: 智能体带薪休假，关掉你的电脑。

turns.en: Let's do it.
turns.zh: 让我们做吧。

turns.en: One last thing I did want to bring up, because this is really impressive: you guys of course are not just working on GrabBot, not just working on the application layer, but also on the model layer and Grok 4.6. The benchmarks came out on Cursor Bench 3.2 and were really impressive, and I wanted to address them here on air while we still have time. You had Grok 4.6 Extra High score 70.8% at an average cost of $2.81 per task. For context, Fable 5 Max scored 70.5% but at $17.32. This is a huge change. How does this model maybe change how the everyday consumer actually interacts with agents, with AI as a whole?
turns.zh: 最后一点我想提一下，因为这真的很厉害：你们当然不只是在做 GrabBot，不只是在做应用层，也在做模型层和 Grok 4.6。基准测试在 Cursor Bench 3.2 上出来了，成绩非常亮眼，我想趁还有时间在节目里聊一聊。Grok 4.6 Extra High 得分 70.8%，平均每个任务成本 2.81 美元。作为对比，Fable 5 Max 得分 70.5%，但成本是 17.32 美元。这是巨大的变化。这个模型可能会怎样改变普通消费者与智能体、与整个 AI 的互动方式？

turns.en: Yeah, go ahead.
turns.zh: 好，你先说。

turns.en: So yeah, this is definitely very top of mind for me because I think about this a lot, since I work at Cursor. I have unlimited tokens, so I can just go crazy with token maxing, but obviously a lot of our customers and our users are more cost-conscious. So personally what I'm most excited about is this idea that you have a very efficient model that is as good as some of the other big models, but at a fraction of the cost. turns.zh: 正如我们在演示中也看到的，编译器还附带一个 ESLint 插件。这样就能在你的编辑器中直接显示编译器诊断信息，这真的很棒。因为这是我们第一次能够在你的代码中显示 React 规则错误。当前的 React ESLint 规则只显示 hooks 规则，这只是我们规则的一个子集。作为发布的一部分，我们还包含一个健康检查脚本，它会让你大致了解采用编译器需要多少努力。当然它并不完美，但它可以给你一些信号，判断这可能需要几天还是几周的努力。所以你们中一些人可能还想知道编译器究竟如何开箱即用地在任何 React 应用上工作。

turns.en: How do we trust it? You don't need to know the theory behind the compiler to use it, but I think it's important to build an intuition for what it's doing. So let's build this intuition by first looking at how we do manual memoization today.
turns.zh: 我们怎么信任它？你不需要了解编译器背后的理论就能使用它，但我认为建立对它行为的直觉很重要。所以我们先来看看今天是怎么手动做记忆化的，以此建立这种直觉。

turns.en: So in today's React, when a component state changes, React is going to rerender that component and all of its children. And this sounds like a lot, and in practice, React is usually fast enough that most of the time it's fine to just rerender. But of course, we all know that there are many occasions as well where rerenders can really hurt performance.
turns.zh: 在今天的 React 里，当一个组件的 state 变化时，React 会重新渲染那个组件及其所有子组件。这听起来很多，而实际上 React 通常足够快，大多数时候直接重新渲染也没问题。但当然，我们都知道也有很多情况下重新渲染确实会严重损害性能。

turns.en: So you don't have to understand all this, but let's take a look at an example and see what the compiler figures out automatically.
turns.zh: 所以你不需要理解所有这些，但我们来看一个例子，看看编译器会自动推断出什么。

turns.en: So first there's a couple of values that don't have any dependencies. These are static so they never need to be recalculated. Then we also have values that depend on the online count here, which is a value that comes from the hook in the first line. And here's something interesting: a value that's cached can also become a dependency of another value.
turns.zh: 首先有几个没有任何依赖的值。它们是静态的，所以永远不需要重新计算。然后还有一些值依赖于这里的 online count，这个值来自第一行的 hook。有趣的是：一个被缓存的值也可以成为另一个值的依赖。

turns.en: Third, we can also have values that depend on the friends prop. And finally, the overall view of JSX that gets returned can also depend on values that are themselves reactive values.
turns.zh: 第三，我们还可能有依赖于 friends prop 的值。最后，返回的整体 JSX 视图也可以依赖于那些本身就是响应式的值。

turns.en: But forget all of those boxes, right? It's kind of confusing. So let's just look at the original code again. This is a really simple example, but it's such a pure description of what your UI looks like.
turns.zh: 但先忘掉那些框框，对吧？有点让人困惑。我们就再看一眼原始代码。这是一个非常简单的例子，但它如此纯粹地描述了你 UI 的样子。

turns.en: So one way to think about the compiler is that it's an auto reactivity compiler. React is too reactive sometimes because when you change anything, everything changes. The compiler now automatically adds just the right amount of reactivity and it makes updates fast by default.
turns.zh: 所以理解编译器的一种方式是，它是一个自动响应式编译器。React 有时过于响应式，因为你改任何东西，所有东西都跟着变。编译器现在会自动加入恰到好处的响应式，并让更新默认就很快。

turns.en: So in React, you describe your UI using plain JavaScript values and the compiler automatically takes care of reactivity and performance for you. So you can forget about reactivity and what you're left with is just React. Yay.
turns.zh: 所以在 React 里，你用普通 JavaScript 值描述 UI，编译器会自动为你处理响应式和性能。于是你可以忘掉响应式，剩下的就只是 React。耶。

turns.en: All right. Another case where you may also need memoization today is if you have expensive calculations. So for example, let's say that you, for whatever reason, need to synchronously process a really large amount of data on the client. And running this function takes a long time. So you don't want to run this repeatedly on every render. So it's really important to memoize this.
turns.zh: 好。今天你可能还需要记忆化的另一种情况是，你有开销很大的计算。比如，假设你出于某种原因需要在客户端同步处理非常大量的数据。运行这个函数要花很长时间。所以你不想在每次渲染时反复运行它。因此对它做记忆化非常重要。

turns.en: The compiler also handles this since you can see that this expensive calculation was used during rendering. And when you combine it with optimizing for rerendering, this is where a really large part of the compiler's performance benefits come from.
turns.zh: 编译器也会处理这一点，因为你可以看到这个昂贵的计算在渲染期间被用到了。当你把它和针对重新渲染的优化结合起来，编译器性能收益的很大一部分就来自这里。

turns.en: One thing to note with this example though: the compiler doesn't memoize everything. It only memoizes React components and hooks. So I mentioned earlier that the compiler understands the rules of React. So ordinary functions which don't abide by those rules are out of scope for the compiler and should be memoized outside of React if they are expensive.
turns.zh: 不过这个例子有一点要注意：编译器不会记忆化所有东西。它只记忆化 React 组件和 hook。所以我前面提到，编译器理解 React 的规则。因此不遵守这些规则的普通函数不在编译器的处理范围内，如果它们开销大，应该在 React 之外做记忆化。

turns.en: So when you combine these two optimizations, automatically figuring out dependencies and reactivity to skip rerendering and memoizing expensive calculations during rendering, the React compiler gets us closer to React's vision, where you continue to work with plain JavaScript values that stay at just the right level of reactivity, making it easy to build great user experiences that start up fast and have responsive interactions.
turns.zh: 所以当你把这两项优化结合起来，自动推断依赖和响应式以跳过重新渲染，以及在渲染期间记忆化昂贵计算，React 编译器让我们更接近 React 的愿景：你继续使用普通 JavaScript 值，它们保持在恰到好处的响应式水平，让你轻松构建启动快、交互响应灵敏的优秀用户体验。

turns.en: If you're interested in gaining a deeper understanding into the many different kinds of optimizations that we do in the compiler, please definitely check out Mofay and Safia's deep dive tomorrow. It's going to be awesome.
turns.zh: 如果你有兴趣更深入地了解我们在编译器里做的许多不同类型的优化，请一定去看明天 Mofay 和 Safia 的深度讲解。会很精彩。

turns.en: But our time together is coming to an end. So here's a slide that you can all tweet. So please check out our docs on the compiler and I hope you have a really good time trying it out.
turns.zh: 但我们在一起的时间快结束了。这里有一张幻灯片，你们都可以发推。请去看看我们关于编译器的文档，希望你们试用得开心。

turns.en: While we wait for the slide to come back. Oh.
turns.zh: 我们等幻灯片切回来。哦。

consensus.en: Grok Bot's design brief was simplicity: chat with agents like colleagues, not micromanage tool calls.
consensus.zh: Grok Bot 的设计要旨是简洁：像与同事聊天一样与智能体交互，而非微观管理工具调用。

consensus.en: Agents with their own computer and persistent identity unlock automation for non-coding roles.
consensus.zh: 拥有独立计算机和持久身份的智能体，为非编程角色解锁了自动化能力。

consensus.en: Grok 4.6 matches top models on Cursor Bench at a fraction of the cost, democratizing agent use.
consensus.zh: Grok 4.6 在 Cursor Bench 上以极低成本媲美顶级模型，使智能体使用民主化。

consensus.en: Engineers become managers of agent fleets, focusing on taste, quality control, and codebase health.
consensus.zh: 工程师转变为智能体团队的管理者，专注于品味、质量控制和代码库健康。

consensus.en: React Compiler auto-memoizes more granularly than humans, making performance automatic and resilient.
consensus.zh: React 编译器比人类更细粒度地自动记忆化，使性能优化自动化且 resilient。

consensus.en: Adopting the compiler requires no rewrites; it safely skips components that break React rules.
consensus.zh: 采用编译器无需重写代码；它会安全跳过违反 React 规则的组件。

contrarian.en: Most AI agent infrastructure for everyday tasks is broken and complex; simplicity is the real differentiator.
contrarian.zh: 大多数面向日常任务的 AI 智能体基础设施既脆弱又复杂；简洁才是真正的差异化优势。

contrarian.en: You don't need to fix all React rule violations before adopting the compiler; it safely skips them.
contrarian.zh: 采用编译器前无需修复所有 React 规则违规；它会安全跳过这些组件。

contrarian.en: Agent PTO: agents don't need rest, but giving them downtime could be a frontier feature.
contrarian.zh: 智能体带薪休假：智能体不需要休息，但给它们停机时间可能成为前沿功能。

contrarian.en: The compiler's memoization is more efficient than manual useMemo, often depending on properties not whole objects.
contrarian.zh: 编译器的记忆化比手动 useMemo 更高效，通常依赖属性而非整个对象。

contrarian.en: Rising AI costs make efficient models like Grok 4.6 a compelling choice over bigger, pricier models.
contrarian.zh: AI 成本上升使 Grok 4.6 等高效模型成为比更大、更贵模型更具吸引力的选择。

contrarian.en: Software engineering demand is increasing, not decreasing, as agents automate more coding.
contrarian.zh: 随着智能体自动化更多编程工作，软件工程需求不降反增。
